item.title: TPE vs PU Rubber Yoga Mats: Which to Choose in 2026
item.description: Cost, grip, eco-profile and which material fits your brand and market.
item.content:encoded:
Originally published at https://sanfan-yoga-site.vercel.app/blog/tpe-vs-pu.html by FUJIAN SANFAN, a yoga mat and foam roller factory in Quanzhou, China.

Materials · 6 min read · Updated Aug 2026

TPE vs PU Rubber Yoga Mats: Which to Choose in 2026

Choosing the right material is the single biggest decision for a private-label yoga mat. Here is how TPE and PU/rubber stack up this year — from a factory that makes both.

What is TPE?

TPE (thermoplastic elastomer) is a lightweight, recyclable, odorless material. Most private-label TPE mats use a double-layer construction — a dense base for support and a textured top for grip — in thicknesses of 4–8 mm. It contains no PVC and no harmful plasticizers.

What is PU / rubber?

A PU mat pairs a polyurethane top layer with a natural-rubber base. The result is exceptional grip, even when wet, which is why it dominates hot-yoga and premium studio lines. The trade-off is weight and a higher unit cost.

Cost and MOQ

TPE is more cost-efficient and friendlier to low MOQs (we start TPE at 100 pcs per design/color). PU/rubber carries a premium price and usually a higher minimum, so it suits established or premium lines.

Grip and use case

TPE gives reliable dry grip for everyday home and gym practice. PU/rubber is the choice for hot yoga, sweaty sessions and studios where slip is not an option.

If you are launching a new brand, TPE is the safer first product. Add a PU/rubber premium line once demand is proven.

Eco profile

TPE is recyclable and PVC-free. Natural rubber is renewable but not recyclable; PU is synthetic. For sustainability messaging, we can advise on recyclable TPE formulations.

Which should your brand choose?

  • New brand / mass market: start with TPE — lower risk, lower cost.
  • Premium studio line: PU/rubber for grip and positioning.
  • Most growing brands: run both, let the market decide.

Not sure which fits your price point? Send us your target retail price and market, and we will recommend a material and spec.

item.title: Yoga Mat MOQ Explained: How Low Can You Go
item.description: What 100-pcs really means for launching and testing a private label.
item.content:encoded:
Originally published at https://sanfan-yoga-site.vercel.app/blog/moq-explained.html by FUJIAN SANFAN, a yoga mat and foam roller factory in Quanzhou, China.

MOQ · 5 min read · Updated Aug 2026

Yoga Mat MOQ Explained: How Low Can You Go

MOQ decides how much cash you tie up before you know if a product sells. Here is what "low MOQ" really means at a factory — and how to use it.

Our MOQ by product

  • TPE yoga mats: 100 pcs per design and color
  • Foam rollers / EVA blocks: 500 pcs
  • Most accessories: 500–1,000 pcs

Why low MOQ matters

A 100-pcs start lets a new brand validate demand without a warehouse of inventory. You can test one color and size, read the market, then reorder what actually sells.

How to use a low MOQ well

Start with a single hero color, confirm quality with a 7-day sample, list it, and only scale once orders come in. Low MOQ turns a bet into an experiment.

Low MOQ is not lower quality — it is better production scheduling. We hold material stock so small runs stay efficient.

Common MOQ myths

  • Lower MOQ ≠ lower quality. It reflects how we batch production.
  • "No MOQ" usually means a trader reselling stock, not a real factory.
  • MOQ is per design/color, so more variants raise the minimum.

Want to plan a launch? Tell us your target quantity and we will map the most cost-effective path from sample to scale.

item.title: REACH, CA Prop 65 & 6P: Yoga Mat Rules for US/EU
item.description: The certifications your importer actually needs — and how we meet them.
item.content:encoded:
Originally published at https://sanfan-yoga-site.vercel.app/blog/compliance.html by FUJIAN SANFAN, a yoga mat and foam roller factory in Quanzhou, China.

Compliance · 6 min read · Updated Aug 2026

REACH, CA Prop 65 & 6P: Yoga Mat Rules for US/EU

Selling into the US or EU means meeting chemical-safety rules. Here is the short list buyers ask about — and the proof a compliant factory should provide.

United States: CA Prop 65 + 6P/7P

California's Prop 65 limits certain chemicals, and US buyers watch phthalate limits (the "6P/7P" list: DEHP, DBP, BBP, DINP, DIDP, DNOP and often DnHP). Mats must be free of these above threshold levels.

European Union: REACH

REACH (Registration, Evaluation, Authorisation and Restriction of Chemicals) restricts Substances of Very High Concern (SVHC). Compliant materials are selected and tested so mats are safe for the EU market.

Our certifications

  • ISO 9001 — quality management system
  • BSCI — social compliance audit
  • Material test reports to REACH / CA Prop 65 / 6P limits
Claims are cheap. Ask any supplier for the actual test report with a date and lab name — not a generic certificate image.

What to ask a supplier

  • Can you provide a recent third-party test report (SGS/TÜV)?
  • Are materials selected for REACH and CA Prop 65 compliance?
  • Is each production batch traceable for re-testing?

We keep material formulations stable and batch-traceable so your compliance holds batch after batch. Request our latest reports any time.

item.title: How to Vet a Chinese Yoga Mat Factory Before Bulk
item.description: Factory vs trader, audits, red flags and what real proof looks like.
item.content:encoded:
Originally published at https://sanfan-yoga-site.vercel.app/blog/vet-factory.html by FUJIAN SANFAN, a yoga mat and foam roller factory in Quanzhou, China.

Sourcing · 6 min read · Updated Aug 2026

How to Vet a Chinese Yoga Mat Factory Before a Bulk Order

Before you commit a bulk order, confirm you are dealing with a real manufacturer — not a trading company reselling someone else's product. Here is how.

Factory vs trader

A factory owns production lines, tooling and QC. A trader sources from factories and resells — adding a margin and a layer of risk. Both can deliver, but a factory gives you direct pricing, faster sampling and real accountability.

Proof a real factory provides

  • Business license with a manufacturing scope
  • Facility photos and video — not just product shots
  • Third-party audit reports (BSCI, SGS, ISO 9001)
  • A live video-call factory tour on request
If a supplier refuses a live video tour or only sends stock photos, that is a red flag.

Red flags to avoid

  • No facility video, or "can't show the floor for confidentiality"
  • Vague answers about production process and capacity
  • Prices that swing wildly with quantity
  • No verifiable export track record

item.title: 7-Day Sampling: Why Fast Prototyping Wins Brands
item.description: How a one-week sample cycle de-risks your launch and beats competitors.

7-Day Sampling: Why Fast Prototyping Wins Private-Label Brands

Speed is a competitive advantage most buyers underestimate. A one-week sample cycle changes how fast you can launch — and how much risk you carry.

What a 7-day sample covers

From your spec, we produce a physical sample with your logo, color and packaging options, then ship it for your review — typically within 7 days.

Why it matters

  • Iterate faster: see and feel the real product before committing a bulk run.
  • Beat competitors: a faster sample-to-shelf cycle wins seasonal and trend windows.
  • Lower risk: fix color, grip or packaging on the sample, not after 5,000 units arrive.
A week to a real, branded sample is the difference between guessing and knowing.

How we do it

In-house tooling, stock material formulations and a dedicated sampling team let us turn a spec into a physical sample in days, not weeks. Custom developments from your sketch or sample follow the same fast path.

Make the most of it

Send your target dimensions, preferred material and brand colors up front. The clearer the brief, the closer the first sample is to production-ready.

item.title: Custom Yoga Mat Sizes & Thickness: A Buyer’s Guide
item.description: Standard, wide, double-wide and non-standard specs — what’s possible.
item.content:encoded:
Originally published at https://sanfan-yoga-site.vercel.app/blog/custom-sizes.html by FUJIAN SANFAN, a yoga mat and foam roller factory in Quanzhou, China.

Customization · 6 min read · Updated Aug 2026

Custom Yoga Mat Sizes & Thickness: A Buyer's Guide

Standard isn't always what your market wants. Here is what is customizable on a yoga mat — and what a flexible factory can actually produce.

Standard sizes

The common format is 1830 × 610 mm (about 72 × 24 in), with thickness from 4 to 8 mm for TPE and up to 12 mm for comfort lines.

Wide & double-wide

We produce 80 cm and 122 cm wide mats, and double-wide formats for partner or family practice — popular with studios and wellness brands.

Thickness options

  • 4–6 mm: portable, close-to-floor feel
  • 6–8 mm: balanced cushion and stability
  • 8–12 mm: extra joint comfort for sensitive knees

Color, double-color & print

Custom Pantone colors, two-tone double-layer looks, and logo printing, embossing or laser engraving on the mat surface and packaging.

Non-standard dimensions? Send your length, width and thickness — we confirm tooling and feasibility before you order.

Packaging & extras

Custom boxes, belly bands, barcodes, QR codes and inserts so your product arrives shelf-ready under your brand.

Share your spec sheet and we will quote a fully customized mat — from material to shelf.
